text: You've proven both Gold tables reconcile. Now it's time to actually point a BI tool at them. This lesson connects Power BI to the Lakehouse for the first time in this course, and loads both gold.daily_sales_summary and gold.category_breakdown into a single report.

Power BI should only ever read from Gold, never Silver or Bronze. Bronze is raw and append-only -- it still carries duplicate transactions from retried ingestion runs, and no business logic has touched it yet. Silver is cleaner, upserted by transaction_id, but it's still row-level transaction detail, and its shape isn't a stable contract -- a data engineer can reshape Silver's intermediate columns without warning anyone downstream. Gold exists specifically to be that stable, pre-aggregated contract a report can depend on, built to exactly the grain each stakeholder actually asked for.

Structurally, here's the connection flow. Get Data, connecting to the Lakehouse's SQL endpoint -- the same endpoint the PySpark and SQL work in this course has been running against all along. In the navigator, select both gold.daily_sales_summary and gold.category_breakdown in that same connection. Then load both into one Power BI data model, rather than building two separate files for two separate stakeholders.

Now the real choice: Import or DirectQuery. Import copies the data into Power BI's own compressed in-memory engine at refresh time, so slicing and filtering stay fast, but the data is only as fresh as the last refresh. DirectQuery sends a live query back to the SQL endpoint on every click, always current, but every interaction now depends on how fast that endpoint answers.

For this pipeline, Import is the right default. Both Gold tables already refresh on the same nightly schedule as the incremental pipeline -- there's no value in querying live between runs, because nothing actually changes until the next run finishes. Import keeps both stakeholder pages fast no matter how much history accumulates in Gold over time, since Power BI's own in-memory engine answers every slicer click, instead of sending that query back to the Lakehouse endpoint. DirectQuery would only earn its cost if Gold needed to reflect changes within a single day, which this pipeline's nightly design simply doesn't call for.

One model, two Gold tables, loaded with Import. Next lesson, you'll build the first of two report pages on top of this model -- starting with Store Operations, the stakeholder this whole capstone began with.
